# Email-address detection

<!-- Generated by node ci/rule-packs/build-detection.mjs --write. -->

Finds bounded ASCII email-shaped values at error severity using the existing example-domain validator. Reports the address location without copying the address into results.

Version: `2026.11.0`. Source: `rule-packs/email.pack.json`.

The citation register records owner approval in principle; legal review remains pending. A finding requests review and does not establish a legal breach.

| Rule | Severity | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| `pii.email` | error | Review protection of identifying email addresses. Sections 24(1)(c), 24(1)(f), 39 and 65; Article 29(1)-(2). |

## Limits

The local part is 1–64 ASCII letters, digits or dot, underscore, percent, plus and hyphen. The domain prefix is 1–64 letters, digits, hyphens or dots and ends in a dot plus a 2–24-letter suffix. This is a detection shape, not full RFC mailbox validation: quoted local parts, internationalised addresses and longer domains are unsupported, and punctuation within a shaped address can be permissive. The email boundary keeps the span inside a longer token: a match cannot start after a punctuation neighbour inside the local part (the oversized-local-part guard), while a sentence-ending dot after the domain does not reject a match. Reserved documentation domains and their subdomains are excluded; the existing synthetic .example corpus domain remains a positive. Public contact and role addresses still require contextual review.

## Remediation and exceptions

Remove unnecessary addresses from fixtures and configuration, replace them with generated test data, and mask addresses in diagnostics. Use the existing justified-exception configuration for deliberately retained public contacts.

## Verification

Run `dotnet test tests/Corpus.Tests -c Release --filter FullyQualifiedName~DetectionPackTests` for exact locations and measured synthetic precision/recall.

These are unsigned release-source packs. Tests sign only in memory with the labelled development key. Production signing, embedding and publication are separate release operations; no development signature is shipped.
